# What can the TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 and LAUNCHXL-F28P65X LaunchPad development kits do, measured from a Mac terminal?

> Disclosure: Fox Red Labs is an independent lab run by a TI employee on personal time. Contributors' projects are their own. Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Texas Instruments or any other manufacturer.

**Short answer.** It builds, loads and runs TI's examples from a Mac terminal with no board changes: 138 of 139 C2000Ware examples for this chip build by script. Do two things first: check the onboard probe's firmware with `xdsdfu -e` and update it if it is older than 3.0.0.43, and use a connection file (`.ccxml`, the file that tells TI's tools which probe and chip to use) that sets the 2-pin cJTAG mode. The motor-control number: a PWM-triggered sample, motor-control step and PWM update takes 2.3 to 2.6 µs.

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md). Every problem hit on this bench, with its cause and fix: [FAQ](FAQ.md). 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. The **probe** is the XDS110 debugger built into the board; **cJTAG** is the 2-wire debug link it uses; the **TMU** is the chip's trig and divide hardware. **CCStudio** is TI's IDE (only its command-line scripting runner was used), **UniFlash** TI's flashing tool, **SysConfig** TI's tool that writes the pin and clock setup code, **C2000Ware** TI's software kit for C2000 chips, and **`ESTOP0`** the C28x instruction where TI's examples stop for a debugger.

## What is in this folder, and what is not

<!-- folder-contents -->
**In this folder:** this README; `AGENTS.md` (notes for an AI assistant, every line from a run); `FAQ.md` and `FAQ-f28p65x.md` (every error hit, with its exact text and the fix); `tools/` (build, load, back-up and restore scripts for these boards, and the two connection files). Results are rows in `data/results/f2800137.csv` and `data/results/f28p65x.csv` at the top of the repository.

**Not in this folder:** TI's SDK, CCStudio, SysConfig and the compilers (you install them; the versions are under "Where these facts come from"); built images (`.out`, `.hex`, `.bin`, `.elf`), which are not cleared for redistribution, so you build them with the command below; raw run logs, which are lab records and not something to run or flash.

**Taking this folder alone:** the commands in this README run from the top of a clone and call `tools/` and `data/`. A sparse clone fetches only those, about 10 to 60 MB, instead of the whole repository (about 500 MB):

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/Fox-Red-Labs/fox-red-labs.git
cd fox-red-labs
git sparse-checkout add c2000-launchpad tools data
```

`docs/` is left out on purpose (236 MB, mostly pictures). Read a page a link points to there with `git show HEAD:docs/<file>`, for example `git show HEAD:docs/vocab.md`.


## The board

| Part | LAUNCHXL-F2800137 | LAUNCHXL-F28P65X |
|---|---|---|
| Chip | TMS320F2800137 (marked `X F2800137PM`, silicon revision B): C28x CPU at 120 MHz with a floating-point unit and the TMU (trig and divide hardware) | TMS320F28P650DK9: dual-core C28x at 200 MHz, one CLA (control law accelerator) per CPU |
| Memory | 256 kB flash, 36 kB RAM | 1.28 MB flash, 248 kB RAM |
| Peripherals | Two 12-bit ADCs, 14 PWM channels, CAN, one motor-encoder input | Not listed here |
| Debugger | Onboard XDS110, 2-pin cJTAG only as shipped | Onboard XDS110 |
| LED | GPIO20 | LED4 on GPIO12 |
| Where to buy | <https://www.ti.com/tool/LAUNCHXL-F2800137> | Not listed here |
| Not on the chip | Not listed here | No radio, no camera interface, no video block |

Sources: `../docs/boards/launchxl-f2800137.json`; user guide SPRUJ32 (<https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/spruj32/spruj32.pdf>); data sheet SPRSP63B (<https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tms320f2800137.pdf>); `AGENTS.md` for the F28P65X rows; `FAQ-f28p65x.md`.

### What was found on the board, and the setting to change

- **The F2800137 probe arrived on firmware 3.0.0.19, and TI's tools would not connect until it was on 3.0.0.43. Tag: Tool or docs.** UniFlash's command line printed `A firmware update is required for the XDS110 probe` and stopped with `Failed: Timed out after 45 seconds`; there is no Update button on the command line.
- **A connection file that leaves the debug mode to the device default fails with error -2131, `Unable to access device register`. Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** Set `SWD Mode Settings` = 4 (cJTAG 2-pin advanced), as TI's `TMS320F2800137_LaunchPad.ccxml` in C2000Ware does; `tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml` is that file plus the test probe's serial number.
- **4-pin JTAG does not work on this board as shipped. Tag: Setup or handling.** The board wires the probe for 2-pin cJTAG only; TDI and TDO need resistors R44 and R45 fitted (user guide SPRUJ32, section 3.2.1).
- **The chip** is marked `X F2800137PM` and reads back as a TMS320F2800137, silicon revision B (`data/chip-id-0x5D008.bin`). It arrived running TI's out-of-box demo; the flash as received is saved in `data/flash-as-received.bin`, read twice with identical hashes.
- **TI's tool warns `Configuring Debugger (may take a few minutes on first launch)...`.** On this bench that step took 1.8 s; the first launch was not timed, so give the first connection a long timeout.

Details and commands for each: [FAQ, Connecting](FAQ.md#connecting).
## Ten-minute path (from a Mac terminal)

The `tools/` scripts are in this repo's `c2000-launchpad/` folder, and they expect CCStudio in `/Applications/ti/ccs2101` and C2000Ware in `/Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00`; edit the paths at the top of each script if yours differ.

1. **Install CCStudio 21.0.1** with every device family, which brings the C2000 compiler and SysConfig: [`../mac-setup/README.md`](../mac-setup/README.md), steps 1 to 5 (about 10 GB of disk).
2. **Get C2000Ware** from TI's public GitHub repo (<https://github.com/TexasInstruments/c2000ware-core-sdk>), only the parts this chip needs. These commands give the same files as the checkout used here (its remote, tag and folder list read back with `git`; an earlier list also named `kernel/freertos_tool`, which does not exist at this tag):

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --depth 1 --sparse --branch REL_C2000Ware_v26.02.00.00.LTS https://github.com/TexasInstruments/c2000ware-core-sdk.git /Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00
```

```bash
git -C /Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00 sparse-checkout set .metadata boards device_support/f280013x driverlib/.meta driverlib/f280013x libraries utilities/clb_tool/clb_syscfg utilities/cmd_tool utilities/dcsm_tool/dcsm_syscfg utilities/transfer
```

3. **Plug in the board and update the probe** if `xdsdfu -e` shows firmware older than 3.0.0.43: the two commands are in the [FAQ](FAQ.md#why-does-tis-software-refuse-to-connect-to-my-launchxl-f2800137-and-how-do-i-update-the-probe). Then put your probe's serial number in place of `CL371081` in `tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml`.
4. **Copy TI's blink example and build it for RAM**, from the `c2000-launchpad/` folder (the build goes into the copy's `build-RAM-Ooff/` folder):

```bash
cp -R /Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00/driverlib/f280013x/examples/led /tmp/led_ex1_blinky
```

```bash
tools/c2kbuild.sh /tmp/led_ex1_blinky RAM
```

5. **Load it and watch the LED pin** (GPIO20, sampled 8 times 250 ms apart):

```bash
/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/scripting/run.sh tools/c2krun.js /tmp/led_ex1_blinky/build-RAM-Ooff/led_ex1_blinky.out blink
```

This is a RAM load: the program is gone at power-off. To keep it, build with `FLASH` in place of `RAM` and run the same command on `build-FLASH-Ooff/led_ex1_blinky.out`; the debugger then writes it to flash. That is how the bench and sweep loaded their flash images; the blink example from flash was not timed.

`c2kbuild.sh` runs SysConfig, compiles with TI's projectspec flags (CPU1_LAUNCHXL configuration) and links. Separate UniFlash command-line calls each reconnect, so they cannot watch a running program; use the scripting runner for that.

For the LAUNCHXL-F28P65X, the same steps use `tools/c2kbuild_f28p65x.sh <example folder> RAM` (CPU1 only) and `tools/c2krun_f28p65x.js <prog>.out blink`, which samples GPIO12 (LED4); its connection file is `tools/F28P650DK9_CL650001.ccxml`. The F28P65X blink was built and seen changed by eye, not timed (results in `data/results/f28p65x.csv`).

## One-command build

From the `c2000-launchpad/` folder, one script runs SysConfig, compiles with TI's projectspec flags (CPU1_LAUNCHXL configuration) and links the copied example (steps 4 and 5 above give the copy and the load):

```bash
tools/c2kbuild.sh /tmp/led_ex1_blinky RAM
```

It took 4.6 s for TI's blink on the F2800137 (observed 2026-10-06; not saved). It does not load the program: use the scripting runner in step 5, because separate UniFlash command-line calls each reconnect and cannot watch a running program. To build every C2000Ware example for the chip, loop `tools/c2kbuild.sh` over the example folders: 138 of 139 build.

## Putting it back on TI's demo

To return the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 to TI's out-of-box demo, write the saved flash image back with `tools/c2kflashback.js` and reset. This was done twice; the flash read back identical to the saved image each time (steps in the [FAQ](FAQ.md#how-do-i-put-the-launchxl-f2800137-back-on-tis-out-of-box-demo-and-how-do-i-know-it-worked)).

## What was measured

LAUNCHXL-F2800137 unless the row says F28P65X. 120 MHz; RAM means code in zero-wait RAM, flash means 2 wait states with TI's prefetch and cache. Cycle counts for math functions include the benchmark loop's own overhead. Sources are rows in `data/results/f2800137.csv` and `data/results/f28p65x.csv`.

| What | Number | Conditions | Level | Source row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blink, TI's `led_ex1_blinky`, terminal build and RAM load | 4.6 s build, 3.9 s load | Observed 2026-10-06, output not saved. Sweep: 4.1 s load and the LED pin seen toggling. Box to blink with a flash write: not measured | measured | `blink_build`, `blink_flash` |
| sinf, atan2f, divide, cycles per loop iteration, TMU flags | 8.0, 17.0, 8.0 from RAM; 12.0, 20.0, 12.0 from flash | Includes 7 (RAM) or 9 (flash) cycles of loop overhead | measured | `math_divide`, `foc_step`, `control_loop`, `isr_entry` |
| sinf, atan2f, divide, C library | 82.0, 697.0, 241.2 from RAM | Same loop | measured | `math_divide`, `foc_step`, `control_loop`, `isr_entry` |
| One field-oriented control (FOC) step, the standard motor-control math, float | 194 cycles with TMU flags (RAM), 221 (flash); 349 without them (RAM) | Per loop iteration | measured | `math_divide`, `foc_step`, `control_loop`, `isr_entry` |
| PWM trigger to new PWM value, FOC step in between | 2.3 to 2.6 µs (means), 12 to 13% of a 50 kHz period; 3.7 to 4.1 µs without the TMU flags | End-of-conversion interrupt; across RAM, flash, and flash with the loop copied to RAM | measured | `math_divide`, `foc_step`, `control_loop`, `isr_entry` |
| CoreMark, patched for the 16-bit byte (**unofficial**) | From flash 141.0 per second, 1.175 per MHz (51% of the MSPM0G3507's 2.30, also from flash); from RAM 155.3, 1.294 per MHz | Unmodified, it does not validate | measured | `coremark`, `dhrystone` |
| Dhrystone 2.1 | 0.362 DMIPS per MHz from flash (50% of the MSPM0L1306's 0.731, also from flash); 0.442 from RAM | Rules followed | measured | `coremark`, `dhrystone` |
| Room-occupancy models occ_cnn_500, 2k, 8k, 30k (636 to 32.8k weights), plain C, from flash | 1.8, 4.8, 17.6, 65.4 ms per inference | 20 of 20 test vectors right in every build | measured | `ai_occ_latency` |
| Same models built by TI's Neural Network Compiler (NNC), from flash | 1.12, 2.60, 9.05, 30.8 ms; 38 to 53% fewer cycles than the fastest plain-C build from flash | 20 of 20 test vectors right | measured | `ai_occ_latency` |
| Float FFT, TI's FPU DSP library | Complex 256 points 0.107 ms; 1,024 points 0.52 ms from RAM, 0.52 to 0.60 ms from flash | | measured | `fft256`, `adc_max_rate` |
| Embench-IoT | 19 of 19 fit and run; 15 pass their own check | | measured | `embench_fit` |
| ADC rate, no wiring | 2.10 million samples a second (Msps) at TI's sample window; 3.98 Msps at 9 cycles | 9 cycles (75 ns) is the data sheet's minimum | measured | `fft256`, `adc_max_rate` |
| TI's C2000Ware examples | 138 of 139 build from a terminal | TI's own flags plus three additions the projects do not list. Running is not passing; most need wiring to show they work | measured | the example build count in this README |
| TI's examples that report fail | 4 clock-check (DCC) examples fail as shipped; all 4 pass with a define or one SysConfig line. All 11 AI examples pass their golden-vector check | | measured | [FAQ](FAQ.md) |
| F28P65X CoreMark, patched | 258.86 per second from RAM (1.294 per MHz); 211.79 from flash (1.059 per MHz) | 200 MHz | measured | `coremark`, `coremark_per_mhz` in `data/results/f28p65x.csv` |
| F28P65X Dhrystone | 0.444 DMIPS per MHz from RAM; 0.279 from flash | TI C2000 compiler -O3, no inlining | measured | `dhrystone` in `data/results/f28p65x.csv` |
| F28P65X room-occupancy models | 0.893 ms (occ_cnn_500) to 47.9 ms (occ_cnn_30k, from flash) | 20 of 20 vectors; occ_cnn_30k did not fit the shared RAM layout | measured | `ai_occ_latency` in `data/results/f28p65x.csv` |
| F28P65X serial port loopback | Clean to 12.5 Mbaud | Internal loopback | measured | `uart_max_clean` in `data/results/f28p65x.csv` |

## If you see this

- If you see `A firmware update is required for the XDS110 probe` and then `Failed: Timed out after 45 seconds` from UniFlash's command line, update the probe with `xdsdfu` (the board arrived on 3.0.0.19; TI's tools need 3.0.0.43). Check first with `xdsdfu -e`. The two update commands are in the [FAQ](FAQ.md#why-does-tis-software-refuse-to-connect-to-my-launchxl-f2800137-and-how-do-i-update-the-probe).
- If you see `Error -2131 @ 0x0) Unable to access device register` from a hand-written connection file, put the property `SWD Mode Settings` = 4 (cJTAG 2-pin advanced) in its connection section, or start from `tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml`.
- If you see `Failed: An invalid processor ID has been found.` on the LAUNCHXL-F28P65X, start from C2000Ware's own `device_support/f28p65x/common/targetConfigs/TMS320F28P650DK9.ccxml`, copy it and add only the probe's serial number ([FAQ-f28p65x.md](FAQ-f28p65x.md)).

The rest of the errors, with causes: [FAQ.md](FAQ.md) (F2800137) and [FAQ-f28p65x.md](FAQ-f28p65x.md) (F28P65X).

## Where to look next

1. [FAQ.md](FAQ.md): every error, with its cause and fix.
2. `data/results/f2800137.csv` and `data/results/f28p65x.csv`: every number on this page, with its conditions.

## Where these facts come from

Checked 2026-10-06 (F2800137) and 2026-10-08 (F28P65X) on an Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9: CCStudio 21.0.1 (C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, SysConfig 1.28.1, scripting), UniFlash 9.6.0, C2000Ware 26.02.00.00 LTS core from TI's public GitHub repo (427 MB on disk including its 87 MB git folder; no myTI login), probe firmware 3.0.0.43. Files: `data/results/f2800137.csv`, `data/results/f28p65x.csv`, `c2000-launchpad/AGENTS.md`, `c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`, `c2000-launchpad/FAQ-f28p65x.md`.

FILE: c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md | What goes wrong with the TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 LaunchPad development kit on a Mac, and how do you fix it?
==============================================================================

# What goes wrong with the TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 LaunchPad development kit on a Mac, and how do you fix it?

Every problem hit bringing up a used TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 (chip TMS320F2800137: C28x core, 120 MHz, 256 kB flash, 36 kB RAM; onboard XDS110 probe) from a Mac terminal on 2026-10-06. Each answer starts with the fix, names what caused it, and quotes the exact error text so a search finds it. Versions: Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9, CCStudio 21.0.1, C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, SysConfig 1.28.1, UniFlash 9.6.0, C2000Ware 26.02.00.00 LTS, probe firmware 3.0.0.43. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

**What caused it**, one tag per answer. The tags used on this page:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Setup or handling | How the hardware was plugged in or set up |
| TI example default | A TI example's default setting is why it fails or misleads |
| Tool or docs | A TI tool bug, a missing tool, or a missing or wrong instruction |
| Chip limit | The hardware cannot do it |
| Third-party behavior | Software from outside TI, such as a benchmark's own check |
| Unknown | Not found; a lead is written as "suspected" |

Contents: [Connecting](#connecting), [Getting the software](#getting-the-software), [Benchmarks](#benchmarks), [Running examples by script](#running-examples-by-script), [The DCC clock examples](#the-dcc-clock-examples), [Neural nets](#neural-nets), [The ADC](#the-adc), [Libraries written for 8-bit bytes](#libraries-written-for-8-bit-bytes).

Words used below (more in [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md)): the **probe** is the XDS110 debugger built into the LaunchPad. **cJTAG** is the 2-wire debug link this board uses. A **connection file** (`.ccxml`) tells TI's tools which probe and chip to use. The **TMU** is the chip's trig and divide hardware. Bring-up records quoted below:.

## Connecting

### Why does TI's software refuse to connect to my LAUNCHXL-F2800137, and how do I update the probe?

Update the probe's firmware with TI's command-line tool `xdsdfu`. The test board arrived on 3.0.0.19 and TI's software would not connect until it was on 3.0.0.43. **Tag: Tool or docs.** UniFlash's command line printed `IcePick_C_0: Warning: A firmware update is required for the XDS110 probe. The current firmware is version 3.0.0.19. The probe must be upgraded to firmware version 3.0.0.43 to be compatible with this software. Click the "Update" button to update the firmware.` and then `Failed: Timed out after 45 seconds`; there is no Update button on the command line. The commands that worked, both in `/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/ccs_base/common/uscif/xds110/`:

```bash
./xdsdfu -I CL371081 -m
```

```bash
./xdsdfu -I 00000000 -f firmware_3.0.0.43.bin -s CL371081 -r
```

The first switches the probe to update mode; the second writes the firmware, puts the serial number back and restarts it. Use your probe's serial number in place of <probe serial>. While the update runs the serial number shows as `00000000`; it came back as <probe serial> afterward. The update itself was observed 2026-10-06 and its output not saved.

### My LAUNCHXL-F2800137 is new. Do I still need the probe update, and how do I check first?

Check first: run `./xdsdfu -e` in the same folder; it lists each XDS110's firmware version and serial number (TI's `XDS110SupportReadMe.pdf` in that folder). **Tag: Tool or docs.** If it is older than what your CCStudio or UniFlash asks for (3.0.0.43 for CCStudio 21.0.1 and UniFlash 9.6.0), update it as above. Only one board, a used one, was tested, so the firmware new boards ship with is unknown.

### Why does UniFlash's command line fail with error -2131 "Unable to access device register" on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137?

Put the property `SWD Mode Settings` = 4 (cJTAG 2-pin advanced) in the connection section of the connection file. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** The device file defaults to cJTAG, but hand-written files failed without the line, from UniFlash 9.6.0's command line, with `fatal: IcePick_C_0: Error connecting to the target: (Error -2131 @ 0x0) Unable to access device register. Reset the device, and retry the operation.` followed by `Failed: Operation was aborted on 'C28xx_CPU1'`. CCStudio's window with a file it generated was not run. TI's own `TMS320F2800137_LaunchPad.ccxml` in C2000Ware has the line and connected first time; `tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml` is that file plus the probe's serial number The console text is saved in.

### Can I use 4-pin JTAG on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137?

No, not as shipped; use cJTAG. **Tag: Setup or handling.** It is how the board is built, not the chip: the board wires the XDS110 for 2-pin cJTAG only, and the TDI and TDO lines on GPIO35 and GPIO37 need resistors R44 and R45 fitted, which the board ships without (user guide SPRUJ32, section 3.2.1).

### TI's tool says `Configuring Debugger (may take a few minutes on first launch)...`. How long does it really take on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137?

On this bench, with TI's connection file, that step took 1.8 s. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The "few minutes" is TI's own warning for a first launch; the first launch was not timed, so leave the first connection a long timeout.

### How do I read which chip and silicon revision my LAUNCHXL-F2800137 has?

Read two registers with UniFlash's command line: PARTIDH at 0x5D00A and REVID at 0x5D00C, two 16-bit words each. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The chip's marking alone does not settle it: the test board's says `X F2800137PM`. It read PARTIDH `0x06FF0500`, which data sheet SPRSP63B lists as the TMS320F2800137, and REVID `0x00000003`, silicon revision B. The command, with your connection file:

```bash
/Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0/deskdb/content/TICloudAgent/osx/ccs_base/DebugServer/bin/DSLite memory -c tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml -r 0x5D008,8 -s 16 -o id.bin
```

It reads 8 words from 0x5D008 (PARTIDL, PARTIDH, REVID) into `id.bin`. The read is saved as `data/chip-id-0x5D008.bin`, with its hex dump in. The X prefix marks a pre-production (TMX) part; the data sheet's "Revision Identification" table lists revision B as available as production TMS parts too.

### How do I run a program and watch the LED from a terminal?

Use the scripting runner. Build with `tools/c2kbuild.sh <folder> RAM`, then run `/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/scripting/run.sh tools/c2krun.js <abs path to .out> blink`. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Separate UniFlash command-line calls each reconnect, so they cannot watch a running program. TI's `led_ex1_blinky` toggled GPIO20 every 500 ms in 8 samples 250 ms apart. This loads the program into RAM, so it is gone at power-off; build with `FLASH` to keep it. `README.md`.

### frl verify says `FRL-E042 UNVERIFIED: only 18 reads a second through the probe`. Is the board wrong?

No: the check could not read the LED pin fast enough to time it. **Tag: Setup or handling.** CCStudio reads this pin about 42 times a second when the computer is quiet; with five other boards writing at once it read 18, below the 20 the check needs, so frl refused to guess. Stop other debug sessions and board runs, then run `frl verify` again. Seen 2026-10-25; `docs/frl.md`.

### How long does it take from box to a blinking LED on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137?

Not measured end to end. **Tag: Unknown.** On first bring-up TI's `led_ex1_blinky` built in 4.6 s and loaded into RAM in 3.9 s (observed 2026-10-06; not saved). That load is not a flash write, so the program is gone at power-off. Before it came the probe firmware update and the first, slow connection, neither timed. A flash write of the blink example was not timed; writing the 256 kB demo image back to flash took 18.6 s and 20.9 s. `README.md`.

### Does it work from CCStudio's window, or on an Apple Silicon Mac?

Not tested. **Tag: Unknown.** Everything here ran from a terminal on an Intel Mac: CCStudio's scripting runner, UniFlash's command line and this repo's build script. CCStudio's window was not used and no Apple Silicon Mac was available.

## Getting the software

### The C2000Ware download on ti.com asks for a login and export approval. Is there another way?

Yes: TI's public GitHub repo has C2000Ware. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The ti.com page does not mention it. A sparse checkout of 26.02.00.00 LTS needed no login and takes 427 MB on disk, including its 87 MB git folder. `README.md`.

### Can TI's Neural Network Compiler (NNC) run on my Mac?

Not on an Intel Mac: NNC 2.1.2 has no Intel Mac build. **Tag: Tool or docs.** It ran on GitHub's Linux machines with the C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS for Linux, from a GitHub Actions job. TI's NNC guide lists Linux and Windows. An Apple Silicon Mac was not run.

## Benchmarks

### Why does CoreMark fail its checks on the TMS320F2800137?

Unmodified, it builds a different-sized workload, because the C28x's smallest memory unit is 16 bits; a three-change patch fixes that, but the score is then unofficial. **Tag: Chip limit.** That applies to the unmodified sources: `char`, `short` and `int` are all 16 bits and `sizeof` counts 16-bit words. Unmodified, three of four result checks fail (`[0]ERROR! list crc 0x0814 - should be 0xe714`, and the same for the matrix and state CRCs) and CoreMark's own type check prints `ERROR: ee_u16 is not a 16b datatype!`; the printed 117.8 iterations per second is not a score. This repo's patch counts the list in 8-bit bytes and masks characters to 8 bits; then all four checks match the standard run. crcfinal depends on the iteration count: 0x4983 at 2k iterations, as on the CC2340R5, and 0xcc42 at 3,000, as on the MSPM0G3507. From flash it scores 141.0 per second (1.175 per MHz), from RAM 155.3, at `--opt_level=4 --opt_for_speed=5`..

### Why does the C2000 compiler say `identifier "int8_t" is undefined`, and why does portable C give different answers on the C28x?

The C28x has no 8-bit type, so TI's `stdint.h` leaves out `int8_t` and `uint8_t`; C2000 compiler 25.11.1 prints `"i8.c", line 2: error: identifier "int8_t" is undefined` for a file that uses it. **Tag: Chip limit.** Add your own `typedef int16_t int8_t;` and check that the code never relies on 8-bit wraparound. The room-occupancy models clamp every value, so they gave 20 of 20 right answers. Every int8 value takes 2 bytes, so int8 weights need twice the flash.

### Why do Embench-IoT's `edn`, `matmult-int` and `picojpeg` fail their own check on the TMS320F2800137?

Not traced; use their cycle counts with care. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** All three do byte or 16-bit integer arithmetic, and they probably assume an 8-bit `char` or a 32-bit `int`, which the C28x does not have. With `st` (next answer) that makes 4 of 19 that fail; 15 of 19 pass. On the MSPM0L1306, 13 of 19 pass, but only 14 fit in its 4 kB of RAM. The build used `CPU_MHZ=1`, which sizes each benchmark's work for a 1 MHz chip, the same setting as on the MSPM0 boards.

### Why does Embench-IoT's `st` fail on the C28x and on the MSPM0 boards?

It fails on all three chips, so it is not the 16-bit byte. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Third-party behavior).** On the MSPM0G3507 it was traced to Embench's 1e-13 tolerance being finer than one step of a double; not traced on the C28x.

### How do I compare a C2000 chip with an Arm chip fairly?

Time the work you care about in cycles, and use the patched CoreMark only with its label. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The [README](README.md) lists CoreMark, Dhrystone, the occupancy models, FFT, Embench and ADC rate, each with its conditions.

### Is the C28x faster or slower than an Arm Cortex-M0+ for my code?

Slower per MHz on general integer code, faster per MHz on float work and on the int8 multiply-adds of small neural nets. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Which chip wins depends on the code you run, so time your own. Chip and compiler are measured together here. Integer, from flash on both: patched CoreMark 1.175 per MHz against 2.30 on the MSPM0G3507, Dhrystone 0.362 against 0.731 on the MSPM0L1306. Multiply-adds: the occupancy networks, which are int8, take 2 to 24% fewer cycles than on the M0+. Float: the networks' quantize step takes about 10 times fewer cycles, and Embench's `minver` 2.4 times fewer, because the C28x has a floating-point unit and the M0+ does not. In seconds, the 120 MHz C28x finishes the models and FFTs well ahead, but the 80 MHz MSPM0G3507 still beats it on CoreMark (183.6 per second against 141.0 from flash) and on several integer Embench benchmarks.

### Why does the TMS320F2800137 need more cycles per byte for AES and per pixel for JPEG than the Arm Cortex-M chips?

Not looked into; if AES or JPEG speed matters, time your own build, and run it from RAM at `--opt_level=4 --opt_for_speed=5`. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** The suspicion: the C28x's smallest data type is 16 bits, and tiny-AES-c and picojpeg are written for 8-bit bytes, so byte work costs extra masking; the generated code was not studied. At -O2 from flash, tiny-AES-c CBC encrypt of 1 kB takes 754 cycles per byte here against 235 on the CC1354P10's Cortex-M33 and 405 to 425 on the Cortex-M0+ chips, and picojpeg 491 cycles per pixel against 178 to 344 on the Arm cores. From RAM at -O4 with speed level 5, AES drops to 395 cycles per byte, level with the M0+ chips, but the Arm builds did not use RAM or a speed option. TI C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS; rows in each board's file in `data/results/`; page.

### Are the AES speed numbers for the F2800137 and the Arm boards like for like?

Nearly: every board runs tiny-AES-c CBC encrypt of 1 kB with the key expanded before the timing starts, and every result matches the standard test vectors. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Two differences remain: the CC2340R5 and CC1354P10 rows take the 1 kB copy into the buffer out of the count (2 to 4 percent of the software time there), while the F2800137 and MSPM0 rows keep it in; and the hardware AES rows on the Arm chips load the key on every call, which is most of the cost for one 16-byte block. The F2800137 has no AES hardware. Rows in `data/results/`.

### How much slower is code in flash than in RAM on the F2800137?

For plain-C programs, 10 to 22% more cycles at 120 MHz. **Tag: Chip limit.** Flash needs 2 wait states at 120 MHz; TI's `Device_init()` sets them and turns on prefetch and the cache. From flash the motor-control (FOC) step took 14% more, CoreMark 10 to 18%, the neural nets 14 to 19%, Dhrystone 22%; single TMU calls 1.5 to 4 cycles more. The whole PWM-triggered loop took only 8% more, because the ADC's sample and conversion take the same time either way. Not always slower: TI's NNC build of one model and the 256-point complex FFT ran faster from flash. Copying the motor-control step and its interrupt to RAM with `#pragma CODE_SECTION(..., ".TI.ramfunc")` brought them back to the RAM time.

### Do I need assembly to use the TMU?

No: it is a compiler option. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Add `--tmu_support=tmu0 --fp_mode=relaxed` to the C2000 compiler's flags, and the compiler turns `sinf`, `cosf`, `atan2f`, `sqrtf` and float divide into TMU instructions. With both flags and code in RAM, sine takes 8 cycles per loop iteration against 82 without either, each including about 7 cycles of loop overhead (9 to 12 from flash). `--fp_mode=relaxed` was not tested on its own, so part of the gain may be that flag.

### How fast can a control loop run on the F2800137?

At 50 kHz a PWM-triggered loop with one field-oriented control (FOC) step uses 12 to 13% of the period with the TMU, 2.3 to 2.6 µs from PWM trigger to new PWM value. **Tag: Setup or handling.** About 66 cycles of that are the ADC's sample and conversion and the interrupt entry; the interrupt code itself takes about 220 cycles from RAM and 243 from flash. Measured with a rate sweep (1,000 periods, none missed), the TMU loop holds 301.5 kHz from flash and 336.1 kHz from RAM, and at 100 kHz it takes 29.7 and 26.4 percent of the CPU; without the TMU 209.4 and 231.7 kHz. A real drive needs time for other work on top.

### How fast can the F2800137 run a digital-power PID loop?

With no missed period in 1,000, the PID loop holds 439.6 kHz in float and 367.0 kHz in Q15 from flash (500.0 and 431.7 kHz from RAM), and at 100 kHz it takes 19.7 and 24.2 percent of the CPU (TI C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS -O2, 120 MHz). Float is faster than Q15 here. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: the C28x's FPU does each float step in one instruction, while 16-bit saturating Q15 arithmetic takes several).** The generated code was not compared.

### Why is the F2800137's highest loop rate lower than its CPU time allows?

From flash the PID interrupt takes 236.5 cycles of CPU (float) and 290.7 (Q15), which alone would allow about 507 and 413 kHz; the sweep found 439.6 and 367.0 kHz. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: the ADC's sample and conversion before the interrupt, and the trigger-to-write time, must fit one period as well).** The FOC loop's flash C-library build, at 209.4 kHz, also came in 5 percent under the 220 kHz estimate, which probably has the same cause: the estimate left out part of the interrupt's return.

### Why is the F2800137 power loop's jitter not quoted?

The first interrupt of each pass in that capture was a stale one, entered with the PWM counter still at 0, so its best case is not real. **Tag: Our mistake.** The program enabled the ADC interrupt without clearing the flag left pending from setup. The worst case and the mean are valid; the rate sweep clears the flag before every trial.

### Why is the ePWM count on the F2800137 not exactly 1,000 per 1k CPU cycles?

Unknown. **Tag: Unknown.** The ePWM clock is set to the CPU clock, and the two flash runs that saved the check counted 991 and 1,005 ePWM counts per 1k CPU cycles; this repo treats ePWM counts as CPU cycles.

### Why does my ADC interrupt read the previous sample when I use the early interrupt?

The early interrupt (`ADC_PULSE_END_OF_ACQ_WIN`) runs your code at the end of the sample window, before the conversion finishes; wait for the conversion before reading the result register, or use the end-of-conversion interrupt. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The test read the result straight away, so in early mode it read the previous sample; it starts the code about 20 cycles sooner (44 to 49 cycles after the trigger against 64 to 70, from RAM). TI's published 49-cycle figure for the F28004x (SPRACW5A) uses early mode.

### Why do the Dhrystone runs on the F2800137 stop at 30,000?

Dhrystone keeps its run count in an `int`, which is 16 bits on the C28x, so it cannot count past 32,767. **Tag: Chip limit.** 30,000 runs take 0.3 to 0.4 s; the timer counts every CPU cycle, so the short run loses no precision. Results: 0.362 DMIPS/MHz from flash, 0.442 from RAM, rules followed.

### Why did the fastest CoreMark build not fit in the F2800137's RAM with a 10 kB stack?

A RAM-only build puts the code, data and stack in the 36 kB of RAM, and the `--opt_for_speed=5` code is 19 kB; cut the stack to 6 kB (CoreMark needs about 4 kB of it) or build for flash. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The 6 kB build used 30.3 kB of RAM and scored 155.3 per second; the flash build of the same setting needs 12.6 kB of RAM..

### Why does my F2800137 RAM build fail with `program will not fit into available memory, or the section contains a call site that requires a trampoline`?

The program is bigger than the 36 kB of RAM: a RAM-only build puts code, constants and stack there. Build for flash, where code and constants sit in the 256 kB and RAM holds only data and stack. **Tag: Chip limit.** The occ_cnn_30k model's weights alone are 65.7 kB, so it cannot run from RAM; from flash it runs in 65 ms. The linker names the section that did not fit: for that model `fails for section ".const" size 0x97de page 0`, 39k words of constants. `fit-check.md`.

### Why does the occ_cnn_8k model not link as a RAM-only image when its weights fit?

The test harness is the cause, not the model: drop the test vectors or build for flash. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The weights are 17.4 kB, but every test image also carries 20 test vectors (10.2 kB) and a 2 kB stack, which together with the code pass 36 kB. Without the vectors it would be about 27 kB, an estimate that was not built.

### Will a 2,048-point float FFT fit on the F2800137?

Probably not with TI's FPU DSP library at its stock settings; none was built. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** A 1,024-point complex FFT used two 8 kB buffers, one starting on a 4,096-word boundary as the library needs, plus a 4 kB twiddle table (the sine and cosine values it multiplies by): 20 kB of the 36 kB. Scaled to 2,048 points that is about 40 kB, and the library's stock tables stop at 1,024 points. A smaller layout, fixed point and another library were not run.

### Why are my FFT timings slower than the cycle counts in TI's DSP library headers?

Measured on this bench, 5 to 17% more cycles than `fpu_cfft.h` and `fpu_rfft.h` list. **Tag: Unknown.** TI does not say where its code and buffers were placed; the measured runs had code and data in RAM, called from C at `-O2`. Results were right (checked against numpy).

### Is FreeRTOS available for the F2800137?

None found. **Tag: Tool or docs.** C2000Ware's public GitHub copy has no `kernel/` folder, C2000Ware's docs list FreeRTOS examples for other C2000 chips but not the F280013x, and upstream FreeRTOS has no C28x port. The full C2000Ware installer, which needs a login, was not checked.

## Running examples by script

### How did you judge whether an example "ran"? Is running the same as working?

No. Running only means it did not crash. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The sweep script loaded each example, let it run 3 seconds, and checked where the CPU was: 114 were still running in normal code, 21 had stopped at their own `ESTOP0` (C2000Ware's "inspect results here" stop), 2 low-power examples could not be halted (see the `Operation was aborted` answer below), and none was in a fault handler. Most drive a peripheral that needs a wire, a second board or a sensor to show they work. Where an example sets its own pass or fail variable, the script reads it.

### Which C2000Ware examples should I never load on a board I want to keep?

`dcsm/dcsm_security_tool`. **Tag: TI example default.** Its image puts data at 0x78000 to 0x78220, the chip's one-time-programmable security area (zone 1 and 2 passwords and settings), and some of those words are not the erased value. Loading it through the debugger's flash tool would program them for good. The sweep's safety check found the sections in the link map and skipped it. Check any image's map for sections outside RAM and main flash (0x80000 to 0x9FFFF) before loading.

### Why does a terminal build of a SysConfig-only C2000Ware example fail with `unresolved symbols remain` for `code_start`?

Add C2000Ware's `device_support/f280013x/common/source/f280013x_codestartbranch.asm`. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** The newer projectspecs list only the example's `.c` and `.syscfg`; the entry branch is not in them and SysConfig does not generate it. CCStudio must add it on import; how was not checked. Also pass `--abi=eabi` (CCStudio adds it for ELF projects) and compile every `.c` SysConfig writes, including its subfolders.

### Why does `transfer_ex2_customlog_export_sci_buffer` fail with `TransferRingBuffer_init` unresolved?

Add C2000Ware's `utilities/transfer/source/transfer_ringbuffer.c` to the build. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** Neither the projectspec nor SysConfig's output lists it. Whether CCStudio's import adds it was not checked.

### How do I put the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 back on TI's out-of-box demo, and how do I know it worked?

Write the flash image you saved on arrival back with `tools/c2kflashback.js`, then reset with `tools/c2krestore.js`. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The script programs main flash only, verifies it, and reads the whole bank back; the readback matched the saved SHA-256 exactly, both times it was done (18.6 s and 20.9 s to write). The demo prints `ADCINA6 Sample` and a reading once a second on `/dev/cu.usbmodemCL3710811` (the probe's first serial port; yours has your probe's serial number) at 115200 baud. If you did not save the flash, rebuild TI's `launchxl_ex1_f2800137_demo` for flash. `README.md`.

### After one example, every later example stops inside `SysCtl_setClock`. Why?

Use a System Reset before loading, not the debugger's default reset. **Tag: Setup or handling.** After TI's `sysctl_ex3_intosc_to_xrosc_config` changed the clock source, the next 7 images all halted in `SysCtl_setClock`; a `System Reset` (`s.target.reset("System Reset")` in CCStudio scripting) cleared it and they ran normally.

### What does `Operation was aborted on 'C28xx_CPU1'` mean when I halt a low-power example?

Probably that the chip is asleep: press the wake-up button or reset. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Setup or handling).** `lpm_ex3_standbywake_gpio` and `lpm_ex5_haltwake_gpio` put the chip in STANDBY or HALT and wait for a GPIO edge, as their source says, and only these two gave the error. The debugger probably cannot halt a sleeping chip; nobody pressed the button to confirm. The debugger reconnected for the next image.

### Is `(Error -261 @ 0x0) Invalid response was received from the XDS110.` fatal?

No. Retry the load. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Setup or handling).** It happened once while the Mac's load average was 78; the same image loaded fine on the next try, and the probe stayed listed by `xdsdfu -e`. Once more the scripting runner exited with no message while loading `hrpwm_ex6_duty_sfo_qformat`; that image also ran fine on retry. `sweep/tools/run_list.py` restarts the runner after either.

### What does `There are not enough resources available` mean when I time code with the debugger's profile clock?

The profile clock and a hardware breakpoint compete for the same debug hardware. **Tag: Setup or handling.** With code in flash every breakpoint is a hardware one. Time with a CPU timer instead: the script starts CPU Timer 1 from the debugger at the breakpoint and reads it after stepping out.

### Why do some C2000Ware examples stop in `verifyEEPROMRead` or set `errorFlag` with nothing else wrong?

They need wiring or a second device. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The I2C EEPROM examples need an EEPROM on the bus, `can_ex5_transmit_receive` needs a CAN bus, and the eQEP, eCAP and external-interrupt examples need jumpers or signals on their pins; each example's comments say which. On a bare LaunchPad they run but have nothing to talk to.

## The DCC clock examples

The DCC (dual-clock comparator) is the chip's block that checks one clock against another. Four of C2000Ware's DCC examples report fail as shipped on this board; all four pass with the changes below.

### Why do TI's DCC examples report fail on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137?

Two causes. `dcc_ex1`, `dcc_ex2` and `dcc_ex4` need the board's crystal turned on, which TI's default clock setup leaves off; `dcc_ex3_continuous_monitoring_of_clock_syscfg` waits for a clock error its settings never cause. **Tag: TI example default.** The fixes, one per example, are in the next three answers. Each crystal example's header says the crystal must be enabled; a script or a newcomer sees only `result` = 1 (fail).

### Why does `dcc_ex1` or `dcc_ex2` stop at `ESTOP0` under the comment `XTAL is not enabled!!`?

Build it with `--define=USE_PLL_SRC_XTAL`, which turns the board's crystal on and runs the clock from it; both then pass. **Tag: TI example default.** C2000Ware's `device.h` runs the PLL from the internal oscillator (`#define USE_PLL_SRC_INTOSC`), so the crystal stays powered down (`XTALCR` = 1 after `Device_init()`). These examples check the crystal first and stop at their own `ESTOP0` with `result` still at its starting value, 1, which they define as fail. In CCStudio, add the define under the project's predefined symbols. From a terminal, with this repo's build script and a copy of the example folder (the third argument is the optimization level, `off` as in TI's project; everything after it goes to the compiler):

```bash
tools/c2kbuild.sh <your copy of dcc_ex1_single_shot_verification> RAM off --define=USE_PLL_SRC_XTAL
```

### Why does `dcc_ex4_clock_fail_detect` pass for the wrong reason?

Build it with `--define=USE_PLL_SRC_XTAL --define=CPU_FRQ_100MHZ`. **Tag: TI example default.** It monitors the PLL as a 100 MHz clock, while TI's `device.h` sets 120 MHz. With only the crystal define, its clock monitor flagged an error before the example turned the crystal off, so its pass did not test anything. With both defines it counted no error until the crystal was turned off, then passed: `tools/c2kbuild.sh <your copy of dcc_ex4_clock_fail_detect> RAM off --define=USE_PLL_SRC_XTAL --define=CPU_FRQ_100MHZ`..

### Why does `dcc_ex3_continuous_monitoring_of_clock_syscfg` report fail when the clock is fine?

Add `dcc1.fclk1 = 100;` to its `.syscfg` file; it needs no crystal. **Tag: TI example default.** Its pass condition is that the monitor fires an error. Its comment says it uses "an un-realistic tolerance" to force an error on a 100 MHz clock, but the SysConfig file leaves the clock at SysConfig's default of 120 MHz with a 3% tolerance, so the window it computes fits the real clock (`DCC_setCounterSeeds(myDCC0_BASE, 3264, 272, 40800)`). With `fclk1` at 100 the error fires and it reports pass. The non-SysConfig `dcc_ex3_continuous_monitoring_of_clock` passes as shipped (`result` = 0).

### Does the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 have a crystal, and what frequency is it?

Yes, Y2, wired to the chip's X1 and X2 pins by default (user guide SPRUJ32, section 3.3.6). Its frequency is assumed to be 20 MHz, not measured. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The user guide does not give the frequency; TI's `device.h` assumes 20 MHz when the crystal is the clock source. With 20 MHz assumed, the DCC read the internal oscillator INTOSC2 at 9.991 MHz and the PLL at 120.13 MHz, close to their nominal 10 and 120 MHz. That shows the three clocks agree; it does not measure the crystal on its own, because the internal oscillator has its own tolerance.

## Neural nets

### What is the room-occupancy model, and why is it the benchmark?

Four small neural nets that count the people in a room (0 to 3) from light, sound, CO2 and motion readings, in sizes from 636 to 33k weights. **Tag: Setup or handling.** They were trained on a public data set for the MSPM0G3507, and the same C source and 20 test vectors run on every board in this project, so their cycle counts compare chips directly. On this chip they take 1.8 to 65 ms from flash as plain C..

### Can TI's Neural Network Compiler (NNC) build my model for the F2800137?

Yes, on Linux or Windows: `tvmc compile --target="c, ti-npu type=soft" --target-c-mcpu=c28` with `--cross-compiler="cl2000"` and the options in TI's NNC user's guide, F28x section. **Tag: Tool or docs.** This chip has no NPU, so use `type=soft`. NNC 2.1.2 has no Intel Mac build, so it ran on GitHub's Linux machines with the C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS for Linux. Place `.rodata.tvm` in flash and `.bss.noinit.tvm` in RAM in the linker file. On the four occupancy models from flash, NNC's code took 38 to 53% fewer cycles than the fastest plain-C build of each (`-O4 --opt_for_speed=5`), and 27 to 29% fewer from RAM on the two that fit there, with every test vector right.

### Why are NNC's memory sizes for the C28x half what the linker map shows in bytes?

NNC counts 16-bit words and calls them bytes: double NNC's figures on the C28x. **Tag: Tool or docs.** For occ_cnn_500 NNC prints `Code: 1647 bytes`; the linker map lists 1,647 for the same library in its own unit, 16-bit words, which is 3.2 kB..

### Does NNC's code need more memory than plain C, and where should it run from?

More memory, and run it from flash. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** Against the plain C builds, NNC's code is 2.3 to 5.4 kB bigger and its buffers 0.5 to 8 kB bigger. For occ_cnn_2k it was slower from RAM (357k cycles) than from flash (312k): in the RAM build the weights, buffers and most of its code landed in the same RAM block, and the CPU probably stalls when it fetches code and reads data from one block in the same cycle. Another RAM layout was not run.

### Why was the washing-machine AI example's feature extraction not timed?

The debugger never stopped at its breakpoint on `FE_runFeatureExtract` within 120 s, although the example passes. **Tag: Unknown.** Not traced; its linker file copies code to RAM, which may move the function after the breakpoint is set. The model call was timed (24.9 ms).

## The ADC

### Can I sample the F2800137's ADC with an 8 or 9-cycle window?

9 cycles yes, 8 no: the data sheet's minimum sample window is 75 ns, which is 9 cycles at 120 MHz. **Tag: Chip limit.** Data sheet SPRSP63B ("ADC Operating Conditions") gives the 75 ns minimum for a source resistance of 50 Ω or less, and a maximum rate of 4 Msps at 120 MHz. Measured on this bench: 3.98 Msps at 9 cycles and 4.12 Msps at 8, so the 8-cycle row is outside the specification. TI's continuous example uses 36 cycles (2.10 Msps). A sensor with a higher source resistance needs a longer window. Accuracy was not measured.

### Why does TI's demo read about 2,000 on pin A6 but your ADC-rate test about 115?

Unknown. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Setup or handling).** Both read pin A6 with nothing connected, and a floating pin has no defined voltage. The two programs sample it differently: TI's demo converts once a second with a 10-cycle window and the ADC clock at SYSCLK/4 (its source, `launchxl_ex1_f2800137_demo.c`); the ADC-rate test converts back to back with 16 chained conversions and the ADC clock at SYSCLK/2. The leftover charge on the sampling capacitor probably sets the reading, but which setting causes the difference was not tested. Connect a known voltage before trusting any reading.

## Libraries written for 8-bit bytes

### Why does a library written for Arm fail on the C28x with `error #20: identifier "uint8_t" is undefined`?

Define `uint8_t` yourself before the library's headers: `typedef unsigned char uint8_t;` (16 bits on the C28x), then check the code never relies on a byte wrapping at 256. **Tag: Chip limit.** The C28x cannot address a single byte, so the C2000 compiler's `stdint.h` leaves out `uint8_t` and `int8_t`. u8g2 2.37.1 printed `"csrc/u8x8.h", line 215: error #20: identifier "uint8_t" is undefined` and 2,701 errors after it; TI's CC1407P host driver printed the same error 445 times from `TRX.h`. C2000Ware's `typedef uint16_t uint8_t;` also clears the error, but breaks u8g2's fonts (next answer). C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, 2026-10-08: [u8g2 experiment](../docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-u8g2.md), [CC1407P host experiment](../docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-cc1407p-host-driver.md).

### Why does u8g2 fail on the C28x with `error #145: a value of type "char [772]" cannot be used to initialize an entity of type "const uint8_t [772]"`?

Define `uint8_t` as `unsigned char` (16 bits on the C28x) for u8g2's files instead of using C2000Ware's `typedef uint16_t uint8_t;`; with that, u8g2 2.37.1 compiles and links unchanged. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** u8g2 stores its fonts as string literals (all 2,174 in 2.37.1's two font files, counted; two were compiled), and C lets a string fill only an array of a character type. Without any `uint8_t`, u8g2 fails earlier with `identifier "uint8_t" is undefined`. Fonts and the frame buffer then take one 16-bit word per byte, twice the memory of a byte-addressed chip. Compile and link check only, C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, 2026-10-08: [u8g2 experiment](../docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-u8g2.md).

### Can TI's BP-CC1407P host driver run on the F2800137? It fails with `error #1167: invalid attribute for "struct TRX_Phy_s"`

Not as it is: even with C2000Ware's `uint8_t` and `-D__packed__=` on the command line, which let all 7 portable files compile, 11 of its 12 message structs come out a different size than the bytes on the SPI wire. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The driver lays its structs straight over SPI buffers, which works only where a byte is 8 bits; a C2000 host needs code that packs each message byte by byte, or a small byte-addressed host (an MSPM0) between the C2000 and the radio. Compile check only, TI Zephyr fork v3.7.0-ti-1.00.01_ga, 2026-10-08: [CC1407P host experiment](../docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-cc1407p-host-driver.md).

### Why does the C2000 compiler print `warning #64-D: shift count is too large` on code that builds clean on Arm?

`int` is 16 bits on the C28x, so `1 << 16` and above overflow; write `1UL << n` (or `1ULL`) for any flag at bit 16 or higher. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The code assumes a 32-bit `int`: TI's CC1407P host driver defines 15 event flags as `(1 << 16)` to `(1 << 30)` and draws 29 of these warnings with the C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS; the same rule is why BitNetMCU needed `1L << shift` above. What the driver's build does with those flags at run time was not checked. [CC1407P host experiment](../docs/experiments/2026-10-08-f2800137-cc1407p-host-driver.md).

## Power measurement and ported examples

### Can I measure the F2800137's current with the kit's own probe, as the MSPM0 LaunchPad does with EnergyTrace?

Not with its own probe; borrow one. The LAUNCHXL-F2800137's XDS110 is a plain debug probe without EnergyTrace hardware: the user guide SPRUJ32 never mentions EnergyTrace, CCStudio's XDS110 driver answers -260 when `tools/energytrace/etcap.py` asks to open probe <probe serial> in EnergyTrace mode, and opened plainly the probe reports hardware id 0x2F, `ET_HardwareInfo` -670, EnergyTrace type 0 (the LP-MSPM0L1306's probe answers 0, type 2, and streams). **Tag: Tool or docs.** Leaving EnergyTrace off a motor-control board is a fair choice, but nothing says so. Two wires from another kit's EnergyTrace probe to the chip side of JP2 make that probe the meter; the first catch is the pin, below, and the second is that the probe is only the meter while it is wired. A bench meter in place of the JP2 +3V3 shunt is the cross-check.

### I power the F2800137 from another board to measure it, and now CCStudio and DSLite say "Error -2131 Unable to access device register". What now?

Flash first, then rewire. With the chip side of the board on outside power (the JP2 +3V3 shunt out, a wire on the chip-side pin) the chip boots and runs, but the board's own XDS110 cannot connect: the scripting runner and DSLite both stop at `IcePick_C_0: Error connecting to the target: (Error -2131 @ 0x0) Unable to access device register`, and a reset press does not help. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: the JTAG level shifters or the probe's target-voltage sense follow the board's own 3.3 V rail).** Put the shunt back, take the wire off, flash, then undo both with the capture already running. One image can carry every phase you want to measure:.

### My STANDBY current on the F2800137 is the same as IDLE. Is STANDBY broken?

No. You re-entered STANDBY too soon after the watchdog wake. The technical reference manual SPRUIX1B section 3.9.4 says, for IDLE, that software must wait for the watchdog's WDINT line to go high again (512 WDCLK cycles) before re-entering; it does not say so for STANDBY, but the rule applies there too. **Tag: Tool or docs.** Re-entering inside that window left the chip in IDLE at 29 mA; a 30 ms wait after the wake interrupt put it in STANDBY at 8.7 mA between wakes, 2.6 mA above HALT.

### Why does the F2800137 read 6.8 mA in HALT when the data sheet promises far less?

Because that reading is not the chip alone. **Tag: Our mistake.** The first profile image entered HALT with the PLL still powered, and the technical reference manual SPRUIX1B section 3.10.4 says to power the PLL down first; with the PLL and both internal oscillators off, HALT reads 6.1 mA, only 0.7 mA less. The rest is everything on the chip side of JP2 that draws with no program running: the CAN transceiver in normal mode, the LED1 power indicator, the encoder buffer. Until a meter on the transceiver splits it, the power rows for this board are quoted "above the HALT reading", not as absolute chip figures.

### Which JP2 pin is the chip side when I wire in outside power?

The lower pin of the +3V3 column, as drawn on the board silkscreen, and it worked on the first try. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: lower pin).** It was not confirmed with a meter; the check is that LED1 lights only when the wire is on the chip-side pin with the shunt out.

### Why does a ported F280015x example fail with `fatal error: cannot open source file "inc/stw_dataTypes.h"`?

The example uses CAN FD (MCAN), and the F2800137 has only the classic DCAN controller, so the F280013x driverlib has no MCAN driver or headers. **Tag: Chip limit.** Use the DCAN examples under `driverlib/f280013x/examples/can` instead. Eleven of the 129 F280015x examples stop here.

### Why does a ported example fail in SysConfig with `cannot set '$assign' to 'EPWM2': No option named EPWM2 defined, valid options are Any EPWM1`?

It asks for high-resolution PWM on a second ePWM module. SysConfig offers high resolution on ePWM1 only for this chip. **Tag: Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** The data sheet says two channels have high resolution; which was not checked. Deleting the fixed pin lines lets SysConfig place two of the nine examples; seven still need a second high-resolution module.

### Why does a ported example fail with `cannot set '$assign' to 'GPIO25'` or `'GPIO30'`?

The F2800137 does not have those pins: neither is in the F280013x `pin_map.h` or on the 64-pin package. **Tag: Chip limit.** Pick another pin in the `.syscfg` file; for the four ePWM digital-compare examples the pin also sits on an input crossbar line, which needs the same change by hand.

### Why does a ported LIN example fail with `identifier "DEVICE_GPIO_CFG_LINTXA" is undefined`?

The F2800137 has no LIN port. **Tag: Chip limit.** There is no port to make; the three LIN examples do not apply.

### Why does `ecap_ex4_sw_sync` fail with `cannot set 'ecapBase' to 'ECAP3_BASE'`?

The F2800137 has two eCAP modules, the F280015x three. **Tag: Chip limit.** Change the third capture to ECAP1 or ECAP2 if the example's logic allows it.

### BitNetMCU on the C28x answers `8888808888` for every digit. What is wrong?

The test digits are stored upstream as hex bytes in a signed array; on a machine where `char` is 16 bits, `0xEC` reads as 236 instead of -20, so every input is wrong and every answer is 8. **Tag: Setup or handling.** Write the digits as signed decimal values (`ports/bitnetmcu/c2000/make_test_data.py` does it) and the answers come out `3209069277`, the same as on a Mac.

### BitNetMCU on the C28x: why `1L << shift` instead of `1 << shift`?

`int` is 16 bits on the C28x, so `1 << 15` and above overflow. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The `L` makes the shift 32-bit. On the test digits the largest shift is 7, so this patch changes no answer; it stops a wrong one on other inputs.

### BitNetMCU on the C28x: why does one buffer carry `aligned(2)`?

The inference code reads the same buffer as 8-bit and as 32-bit words. On the C28x a 32-bit read needs an even word address. **Tag: Setup or handling.** The compiler placed it on one anyway; the attribute makes that certain across builds.

### tiny-AES-c gives the wrong ciphertext on the TMS320F2800137, and FIPS-197 C.1 fails. Why?

Mask the result of tiny-AES-c's `xtime()` to 8 bits (`& 0xFF`); with that one line changed, all 9 checks in this repo's test pass on the chip. **Tag: Third-party behavior.** tiny-AES-c expects a `uint8_t` to drop its top bit when it shifts left, which is true on an 8-bit-byte chip. On the C28x the smallest type is 16 bits, so the bit stays, the next S-box lookup reads past the end of the table, and the cipher comes out wrong. A Mac build with a 16-bit `uint8_t` shows the same failure and the same fix. This repo's `build.sh` patches a copy and leaves the vendored source untouched. TI C2000 compiler 25.11.1, tiny-AES-c commit 2385675; results in.

### TI's CC1407P host driver fails on the C28x with `uint8_t` undefined and `invalid attribute for "struct TRX_Phy_s"`. How do I build it?

Pass `portability/cc1407p-host/c28x/c28x_compat.h` with `--preinclude`: it defines `uint8_t` as a 16-bit `unsigned char` and `__packed__` as empty. All files then compile with no change to TI's code. **Tag: Chip limit.** The build is not the end: run on the board, the driver's first SPI message is 9 units against the Arm build's 10 bytes, because structs laid over the SPI buffer take a 16-bit word per member. If you see `TRX_Host_open` never return, that is why; write a field-by-field packer (`portability/cc1407p-host/c28x/README.md`).

### Why does the CC1407P host driver's `LRF_*_byteCount` come out half as big on the C28x?

It is `sizeof` of a `uint32_t` array, and `sizeof` counts 16-bit words here. **Tag: Setup or handling.** A 68-entry table reports 136, not 272. Use 4 octets per entry with `portability/cc1407p-host/wire/trx_wire.c` (`trx_w_words_to_octets`), which also packs every other message field by field; 17 of 17 cases equal TI's structs on a Mac and on this board (run 2026-10-25, `docs/experiments/2026-10-25-f2800137-cc1407p-wire-packer.md`).

### Does the portable three-ways app run here without editing it?

Yes, with one preinclude. **Tag: Setup or handling.** `app.h` uses `uint8_t`, which the C28x `stdint.h` omits; `portability/three-ways/c2000/c28x_preinclude.h` supplies it for `app.c` only (C2000Ware's driverlib headers already define `uint8_t`, so the glue file must not get it). 35 glue lines, 29 config lines, 4.9 kB code, 1.0 kB RAM, serial check passes at 115200 (`portability/three-ways/c2000/README.md`).

<!-- recovery:start -->
## When the board stops answering

Checked 2026-10-24. Before flashing a risky image, run `python3 tools/preflight_image.py <board id> <image.out>`. Narrative and commands: `docs/remote-board-recovery.md`.

**LAUNCHXL-F2800137**

No lockup is recorded for this board.

**LAUNCHXL-F28P65X**

No lockup is recorded for this board.

FILE: c2000-launchpad/AGENTS.md | What should an AI coding assistant know before working on a TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 or LAUNCHXL-F28P65X LaunchPad development kit?
==============================================================================

# What should an AI coding assistant know before working on a TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137 or LAUNCHXL-F28P65X LaunchPad development kit?

Short answer: a C2000 byte is 16 bits, so portable Arm code breaks in quiet ways (missing `uint8_t`, wrong checksums, shifts that overflow), and that TI's debug tools on a Mac need a matching probe firmware and a connection file made for the exact chip. This file is the short list. Each item comes from runs on these boards unless it says otherwise.

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md), the [LAUNCHXL-F2800137 FAQ](FAQ.md) and the [LAUNCHXL-F28P65X FAQ](FAQ-f28p65x.md) in the Fox Red Labs repo. In short: the **probe** is the XDS110 debugger built into the board; a **connection file** (`.ccxml`) tells TI's tools which probe and chip to use; the **TMU** is the F2800137's trig and divide hardware; **SysConfig** is TI's tool that writes pin and clock setup code; **C2000Ware** is TI's software kit for C2000 chips; **CoreMark** is a standard CPU speed test; **PIE** is the interrupt controller that routes peripheral lines to the CPU; **CLA** is a second, smaller processor on some C2000 chips. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. Checked 2026-10-06 (F2800137) and 2026-10-08 (F28P65X) on an Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9, with CCStudio 21.0.1, C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, C2000Ware 26.02.00.00 LTS, UniFlash 9.6.0 and probe firmware 3.0.0.43, on one board of each.

**How to use it.** Copy this file into the top folder of your own project as `AGENTS.md`. Most coding assistants read that name; for one that reads `CLAUDE.md`, copy it under that name or add the line `@AGENTS.md` to your `CLAUDE.md`. Paths below in backticks starting `c2000-launchpad/` are in the Fox Red Labs repo, where the evidence for each line lives; they are not in your copy, and links in this file only work inside that repo.

## What both boards share

| Part | Fact |
|---|---|
| CPU | C28x core with floating-point unit; `char`, `short` and `int` are all 16 bits and `sizeof` counts 16-bit words (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`) |
| Debugger | XDS110 on the board, USB; the F2800137 is wired for 2-pin cJTAG only (4-pin needs R44 and R45 fitted) (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`) |
| Compiler flags used | `-v28 -ml -mt --float_support=fpu64 --abi=eabi` |

## Start here

Built and checked with CCStudio 21.0.1, C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, SysConfig 1.28.1, C2000Ware 26.02.00.00 LTS, UniFlash 9.6.0 and probe firmware 3.0.0.43. The `tools/` scripts expect CCStudio in `/Applications/ti/ccs2101` and C2000Ware in `/Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00`; set `TI_ROOT` to the folder that holds them if yours differ (`c2kbuild_f28p65x.sh`; `c2kbuild.sh` reads `C2000WARE` or you edit its top lines). Find the probe serial with `xdsdfu -e` (in CCStudio's `ccs_base/common/uscif/xds110/` folder). Put it in place of `CL371081` in `c2000-launchpad/tools/F2800137_CL371081.ccxml` (F2800137) or the serial in `c2000-launchpad/tools/F28P650DK9_CL650001.ccxml` (F28P65X).

| Step | LAUNCHXL-F2800137 | LAUNCHXL-F28P65X |
|---|---|---|
| Backup | No script. The flash was saved on arrival: 0x20000 words from 0x80000, read twice, identical SHA-256 (`c2000-launchpad/data/flash-as-received.bin`). The scripting call that reads it is `s.memory.saveBinary(0x80000, 0x20000, <file>.bin)` | No tested backup command |
| Build | `cp -R /Applications/ti/c2000ware_core_26_02_00_00/driverlib/f280013x/examples/led /tmp/led_ex1_blinky` then `c2000-launchpad/tools/c2kbuild.sh /tmp/led_ex1_blinky RAM` | `c2000-launchpad/tools/c2kbuild_f28p65x.sh <example folder> RAM` (CPU1 only; finds CCStudio and C2000Ware under `TI_ROOT`, default `/Applications/ti`, or from `C2000WARE`, `CGT` and `SYSCFG`, and says which one is missing) |
| Load and check | `/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/scripting/run.sh c2000-launchpad/tools/c2krun.js /tmp/led_ex1_blinky/build-RAM-Ooff/led_ex1_blinky.out blink` samples GPIO20 eight times | `/Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/scripting/run.sh c2000-launchpad/tools/c2krun_f28p65x.js <prog>.out blink` samples GPIO12 (LED4) |
| Keep after power-off | Build with `FLASH` in place of `RAM` and run the same command | Same, with `FLASH` |
| Restore | `run.sh c2000-launchpad/tools/c2kflashback.js <abs>/flash-as-received.bin <abs>/<readback>.bin`, then `run.sh c2000-launchpad/tools/c2krestore.js`. Verified twice | Not tested |

A RAM load is gone at power-off. Separate UniFlash command-line calls each reconnect, so use the scripting runner to watch a running program. The F2800137 blink built in 4.6 s and loaded in 3.9 s; the F28P65X blink was built and seen changed by eye, not timed.

## If you see this

| What you see | Cause | Do this | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error #20: identifier "uint8_t" is undefined` | The C28x cannot address a byte, so TI's `stdint.h` omits `int8_t` and `uint8_t` | Put `typedef unsigned char uint8_t;` before the library's headers | The file compiles |
| `error #145: a value of type "char [772]" cannot be used to initialize an entity of type "const uint8_t [772]"` (u8g2) | C2000Ware's `typedef uint16_t uint8_t;` clears error #20 but breaks the fonts | Use the `unsigned char` typedef, not the `uint16_t` one | The fonts compile |
| `warning #64-D: shift count is too large` | `int` is 16 bits | Write `1UL << n` (`1L << shift` in BitNetMCU) | No warning |
| `ERROR: ee_u16 is not a 16b datatype!` | Unmodified CoreMark assumes bytes | Use this repo's three-change patch; the score is then unofficial | CoreMark validates |
| `unresolved symbols remain` naming `code_start` (F2800137) | A SysConfig-only example's entry branch is not generated | Add `f280013x_codestartbranch.asm`, `--abi=eabi` and every `.c` SysConfig writes | The link succeeds |
| `unresolved symbols remain` naming `TransferRingBuffer_init` | `transfer_ringbuffer.c` is in neither the projectspec nor SysConfig output | Add `utilities/transfer/source/transfer_ringbuffer.c` | The link succeeds |
| `Operation was aborted on 'C28xx_CPU1'` on `lpm_ex3_standbywake_gpio` or `lpm_ex5_haltwake_gpio` | The chip is asleep and cannot be halted | Press the wake-up button or reset | The debugger reconnects |
| `(Error -261 @ 0x0) Invalid response was received from the XDS110.` | Seen once under heavy Mac load | Retry the load | The same image loads |
| `There are not enough resources available` | The profile clock and a hardware breakpoint share debug hardware | Time with a CPU timer instead | The cycle count prints |
| `fatal error: cannot open source file "inc/stw_dataTypes.h"` | A ported F280015x MCAN example; the F2800137 has no MCAN | Do not port it | Not applicable |
| `cannot set '$assign' to 'EPWM2'`, `'GPIO25'`, `'GPIO30'` or `cannot set 'ecapBase' to 'ECAP3_BASE'` | The F2800137 lacks those parts | Pick pins and modules this chip has | SysConfig accepts it |
| `invalid attribute for "struct TRX_Phy_s"` with `uint8_t` undefined (TI CC1407P host driver) | `__attribute__((__packed__))` written directly in TRX.h; no 8-bit type | `--preinclude` `portability/cc1407p-host/c28x/c28x_compat.h`; it builds, but the message bytes are still wrong on a 16-bit char (run 2026-10-24: 9 units sent against 10 bytes), so add a field-by-field packer | 12 of 12 files compile; CRC-16 of `123456789` is 0x29B1 |
| The CC1407P host driver sends different bytes than on Arm, or `LRF_*_byteCount` is half what you expect | Structs and bit-fields laid over the SPI buffer assume 8-bit bytes; `sizeof` counts 16-bit words | Use the field-by-field packer `portability/cc1407p-host/wire/trx_wire.c` (run 2026-10-25: 17 of 17 cases equal, 315 octets, same digest as a Mac) | The stream digest DC1DF5B1 matches |
| `error: invalid redeclaration of type name "uint8_t"` when preincluding a `uint8_t` typedef into a file that includes driverlib | `driverlib/inc/hw_types.h` already defines `uint8_t` | Preinclude only the files that do not include driverlib (`portability/three-ways/c2000/build.sh`, run 2026-10-25) | The file compiles |
| `8888808888` for every digit (BitNetMCU), or a wrong tiny-AES-c ciphertext | Code assumes a byte wraps at 256 | Write the test digits as signed decimals; mask `xtime()` with `& 0xFF` | Digits differ; FIPS-197 C.1 passes |

Traps shared with other boards: TRAPS.md.

## Traps on both boards

1. **Check a ported constant against this chip's own header.** Interrupt macros keep their names across chips and change their values (see the F28P65X section).
2. **Check an image's map for sections outside RAM and main flash before loading it.** `dcsm/dcsm_security_tool` puts data in the one-time-programmable security area at 0x78000 and was skipped (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`).

## LAUNCHXL-F2800137

| Part | Fact |
|---|---|
| Chip | TMS320F2800137, 120 MHz, 256 kB flash, 36 kB RAM, TMU, two 12-bit ADCs, 14 PWM channels, CAN (classic DCAN, no CAN FD), no LIN port, two eCAP modules (`c2000-launchpad/README.md`, `c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`) |
| LED | TI's blink toggles GPIO20 (`c2000-launchpad/README.md`) |
| Crystal | Y2 on X1 and X2; 20 MHz is assumed by TI's `device.h`, not measured |
| Not on the chip | No AES hardware, no FreeRTOS in C2000Ware's public copy for this chip |

- **TMU.** Add `--tmu_support=tmu0 --fp_mode=relaxed`; sine takes 8 cycles per loop iteration against 82 without (`data/results/f2800137.csv`).
- **Flash is 10 to 22% slower than RAM** at 120 MHz (2 wait states) (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`).
- **TI's DCC examples** report fail as shipped; build with `--define=USE_PLL_SRC_XTAL` (ex1, ex2, ex4 also `--define=CPU_FRQ_100MHZ`) or add `dcc1.fclk1 = 100;` (ex3 syscfg).
- **Read chip identity** from PARTIDH 0x5D00A and REVID 0x5D00C: the chip here read `0x06FF0500` and revision B (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`).

## LAUNCHXL-F28P65X

| Part | Fact |
|---|---|
| Chip | TMS320F28P650DK9, dual-core C28x at 200 MHz, 1.28 MB flash, 248 kB RAM, one CLA per CPU |
| LED | LED4 on GPIO12 (`data/results/f28p65x.csv`) |
| Not on the chip | No radio, no camera interface, no video block |

- **Ported interrupt test never fires.** `INT_FREERTOS` is PIE group 12 line 12 here (`0x00DB0C0CU`, low byte line, next byte group), line 6 on the F2800137. No compiler error (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ-f28p65x.md`).
- **Only CPU1 and C28x-only builds were run.** CPU2 and the CLA are untouched.

## What ran here

- F2800137, blink: 4.6 s build, 3.9 s RAM load; box to blink with a flash write not measured (`c2000-launchpad/FAQ.md`).
- F2800137, FOC step with TMU: 194 cycles from RAM, 221 from flash; PWM trigger to new PWM value 2.3 to 2.6 µs (`data/results/f2800137.csv`).
- F2800137, patched CoreMark: 141.0 per second from flash (1.175 per MHz), 155.3 from RAM; Dhrystone 0.362 DMIPS per MHz from flash (`data/results/f2800137.csv`).
- F2800137, occupancy models 500 to 30k: 1.8 to 65.4 ms plain C from flash, 20 of 20 vectors (`data/results/f2800137.csv`).
- F2800137, TI examples: 138 of 139 build from a terminal.
- F28P65X, patched CoreMark: 258.86 per second from RAM (1.294 per MHz), 211.79 from flash; SCI loopback clean to 12.5 Mbaud (`data/results/f28p65x.csv`).
- F28P65X, occupancy models: 0.893 ms to 47.9 ms, 20 of 20 vectors; `occ_cnn_30k` did not fit the shared RAM layout and ran from flash (`data/results/f28p65x.csv`).

## Ports that ran here

Code written for other chips and tools, brought to this board. The files to copy, the command and what you see for each are in `docs/ports.md`; the method and a prompt to port your own are there too. Works ran and did what it should; Could work ran in part.

| Port | Status | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| BitNetMCU on a C2000 control chip (LAUNCHXL-F2800137) | Works | BitNetMCU's 64-wide CNN reads all 10 test digits right on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137. | `ports/bitnetmcu/README.md` |

| ESP32-BLE-Gamepad (a Bluetooth HID gamepad library) on TI, ST and C2000 boards | Works | The ESP32-BLE-Gamepad descriptor and reports match the library's output byte for byte on four boards, and 15 of 15 button changes from the LP-EM-CC2340R5 reached a Mac as gamepad reports. | `docs/experiments/2026-10-19-esp32-ble-gamepad-port-matrix.md` |
| CC1407P host driver on the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 | Could work | The CC1407P driver files compile for the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 with a compatibility header, and a field-by-field packer gives the same 315 octets as an Arm host. | `docs/experiments/2026-10-25-f2800137-cc1407p-wire-packer.md` |

==============================================================================
FILE: c2000-launchpad/FAQ-f28p65x.md | What goes wrong with the TI LAUNCHXL-F28P65X LaunchPad development kit on a Mac, and how do you fix it?
==============================================================================

# What goes wrong with the TI LAUNCHXL-F28P65X LaunchPad development kit on a Mac, and how do you fix it?

Every problem hit while bringing up a new TI LAUNCHXL-F28P65X (chip TMS320F28P650DK9: dual-core C28x, 200 MHz, 1.28 MB flash, 248 kB RAM; onboard XDS110 probe) from a Mac terminal on 2026-10-08. Each answer starts with the fix, names what caused it, and quotes the exact error text so a search finds it. Versions: Intel Mac, macOS 15.7.9, CCStudio 21.0.1, C2000 compiler 25.11.1.LTS, C2000Ware 26.02.00.00 LTS, probe firmware 3.0.0.43. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes. This board shares most of its tooling with the TI LAUNCHXL-F2800137; see that board's own FAQ for problems common to C2000 LaunchPad development kits in general.

**What caused it**, one tag per answer. The tags used on this page:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Setup or handling | How the hardware was plugged in or set up |
| Tool or docs | A TI tool bug, a missing tool, or a missing or wrong instruction |
| Chip limit | The hardware cannot do it |

Words used below (more in [docs/vocab.md](../docs/vocab.md)): the **probe** is the XDS110 debugger built into the LaunchPad. A **connection file** (`.ccxml`) tells TI's tools which probe and chip to use. The **PIE** is the C28x's interrupt controller that routes peripheral lines to the CPU. The **CLA** is a second, smaller processor on some C2000 chips, one per CPU on this one; nothing on this page uses it.

Board overview and measured numbers: [README](README.md). Contents: [Connecting](#connecting), [Porting from another C2000 chip](#porting-from-another-c2000-chip).

## Connecting

### My hand-written connection file fails every operation with "An invalid processor ID has been found." What is wrong?

Start from TI's own connection file for this chip, not a single-core board's file. **Tag: Tool or docs.** This chip adds a second processor (a CLA, control law accelerator) on each of its two CPUs, and a connection file built the way a single-core C2000 board's is (one entry pointing at the device database) fails every operation, including a plain probe identify, with `Failed: An invalid processor ID has been found.` The fix is C2000Ware's own file, `device_support/f28p65x/common/targetConfigs/TMS320F28P650DK9.ccxml`: copy it and add only the probe's serial number. It adds one driver line the single-core template lacks (`drivers/tixds510cla2.xml`) and narrows the connection to one subpath instead of the full default device tree.

### My probe's firmware is below 3.0.0.43. Do I need to update it for this error?

No, not for this one. **Tag: Tool or docs.** The probe's firmware was updated from 3.0.0.26 to 3.0.0.43 along the way (the same update the F2800137 needed, with TI's `xdsdfu` tool), and the "invalid processor ID" error was unchanged before and after. The fix is the connection file above, not the firmware. Update the firmware anyway: CCStudio 21.0.1 and UniFlash 9.6.0 ask for 3.0.0.43 or newer before they will do anything else.

## Porting from another C2000 chip

### I ported a test from another C2000 board. It builds and runs with no error, but it never does the one thing it is supposed to measure

Check whether the test pends an interrupt by writing a specific bit number, and reread this chip's own `hw_ints.h` before trusting that number. **Tag: Chip limit.** An interrupt-latency test was ported from the LAUNCHXL-F2800137 that forces its own spare interrupt (`INT_FREERTOS`) from software, by writing a hard-coded PIE flag bit, to time how long the CPU takes to reach the handler. On the F2800137 that interrupt is PIE group 12, line 6. On this chip it is PIE group 12, line 12 (`driverlib/f28p65x/driverlib/inc/hw_ints.h`, `INT_FREERTOS 0x00DB0C0CU`). The program linked, ran and reported a clean result, except the result was always "zero samples": the handler never fired, because the test was pending bit 6 while the chip's own vector table was listening on bit 12. There is no compiler error for this, because the macro name is the same on both chips and only its value differs. To find the real line for any `INT_xxx` macro, read the macro's own value: the low byte is the line, the next byte the group (`0x00DB0C0CU` decodes to line 12, group 12).
